result.topic_en: Riemann bounds from below the integral L (the Dirichlet-type integral for the minimum problem) using the minimal value of a one-dimensional integral. He gives Weierstrass-style counterexamples showing that L can be made small when the function has discontinuities, and modifies the claim about the existence of the minimum of Omega accordingly.

items.english: The minimum of Omega does not necessarily occur for one of the functions lambda. In any case, however, it then occurs for a function affected by a removable discontinuity.

Punkte $O'$ einer endlichen Größe $a$ gleich sein solle,

items.english: Requiring that lambda be 0 on the boundary and equal to a finite quantity a at a point O' does not prevent L from being made smaller than any given quantity.
